title: Bekal Fort not tall enough to hide murky beach fest deals; more skeletons tumble out
content: Kasaragod: Replying to an RTI application, the Bekal Resorts Development Corporation (BRDC) has denied releasing any money to former Kasaragod District Congress president Hakkeem Kunnil from either its own account or that of the Bekal International Beach Fest organising committee, then headed by Udma MLA and CPM leader CH Kunhambu. ​But bank records and the organising committee's cheque issue register show that the committee paid 10.46 lakh to the Congress leader, 8.46 lakh of which was used to clear the Congress leader's gold loan. The denial of BRDC, a government agency at the centre of the alleged beach festival scam, is also at odds with Kunnil's own account of the transaction and Kunhambu's confirmation that the committee had borrowed money from him and repaid it with interest. ​The revelation, the subsequent denial and the discrepancy come against the backdrop of a Vigilance inquiry into the handling of Bekal International Beach Fest funds during its first three editions, held under the LDF government in 2022-23, 2023-24 and 2024-25. Despite the huge public response, the first edition of the year-end festival was marred by allegations of massive underreporting of revenue and visitor numbers, as well as the sale of fake tickets. ​The second edition was also sullied by allegations of fake ticket sales, and BRDC releasing 50 lakh to the organising committee to cover up an alleged loss of 86 lakh in June 2024, despite objections from its finance manager. The corporation's independent auditors, Chennai-based Rajesh and Ganesh, subsequently reported that the 50-lakh expenditure was not approved or budgeted by the management and that no supporting bills or statements were furnished. According to Kunhambu and BRDC officials, the 10.46 lakh paid in connection with Kunnil's loans was drawn from this 50 lakh. ​The RTI reply was signed by BRDC's Personnel and Administration Manager Prasad U S, who had earlier told applicants that BRDC had no access to the organising committee's accounts. Though the government authorised BRDC to organise the beach fest, it was organised by a people's committee led by LDF leaders, with BRDC's MD serving as the festival's chief coordinator. 'Money raised from committee members' When contacted, Kunhambu said there was a shortfall of around 40 lakh during the second edition, and a core team of the organising committee had temporarily arranged the money. "I contributed 5 lakh, I think. Another person contributed 10 lakh, BRDC MD (P Shijin) 10 lakh, and Hakeem another 10 lakh. M A Latheef from our INL also contributed," Kunhambu said. ​"BRDC released the money to us only after the accounts were audited and submitted," he said. But BRDC's independent auditors had flagged the 50 lakh spend as per its report accessed by Onmanorama. ​Hakkeem Kunnil told Onmanorama that he first loaned 2 lakh to the organising committee for a week and then pledged his wife's gold at the CPM-run Pallikkere Service Co-operative Bank's evening branch at Pallikkara to raise another 8 lakh for the fest. "I gave the money in cash, and I was repaid in cash after six months," he said. ​According to bank receipts, Hakkeem had pledged the gold jewellery at an interest rate of 9.7% for six months on December 26, 2023. The loan was closed nearly seven months later, after payment of the interest, a 2% late fee and bank charges of 46,481. ​One of Kunhambu's arguments was that the organising committee had borrowed money from its members because it lacked funds to pay performers, particularly singers KS Chithra and MG Sreekumar, who performed on December 24 and 25, 2023. ​BRDC Finance Manager Ajith Kumar, however, said Chithra's concert had generated 13 lakh from counter ticket sales alone, and the cash was kept at the BRDC office. There was also money in the organising committee's bank account, he said. Chithra had claimed on Facebook that around 65,000 people attended her December 24 concert...
